name: Kon Tum
provinceNote: Kon Tum city and the former Kon Tum province merged into Quảng Ngãi on 1 July 2025. The provincial capital is Quảng Ngãi city. Kon Tum remains the highland city travelers mean on the map.
dotReason: Worth it for Central Highlands culture
summary: You come for the timber cathedral on Nguyen Hue, built in cà chít wood from 1913 to 1918, and for the afternoon across the Đăk Bla at Kon Klor. Stay when that church and the Ba Na villages are the trip. Choose Da Lat when you wanted a cooler hill station instead.
timeNeeded: 1–2 days for the church, the prison, and Kon Klor
fee: No single city ticket. Sights bill separately.
getThere: Pleiku Airport (PXU), then the road. kontumtourism.com prints nearly 45 km and about one hour. Travelmath prints 51 km.
seoTitle: Kon Tum travel guide — timber church on Nguyen Hue
seoDescription: The 1913 timber cathedral stands on Nguyen Hue, and Kon Klor’s 292-metre bridge crosses the Đăk Bla. Fly to Pleiku: nearly 45 km, or 51 km by road.
intro: Breakfast is phở khô in two bowls, noodles in one and hot broth in the other. Go Vietnam puts those shops at roughly 06:00 to 10:00, on streets near the market, at about 20,000–33,000 VND a bowl, or up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl. Then you walk Nguyen Hue. The Kon Tum provincial portal places the wooden cathedral in Thống Nhất ward, built from 1913 to 1918 in cà chít timber, with Roman lines and Ba Na roof forms. Go Vietnam lists free entry and Sunday Mass at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00. Hours outside Mass are Check on arrival. Give the church about an hour.

Give the afternoon to Kon Klor. The cable bridge opened on 1 May 1994 and runs 292 metres over the Đăk Bla. Go Vietnam’s cluster page and its Kon Klor communal-house page both print that length. The nhà rông beside the river is the large Ba Na hall, rebuilt after the 2010 fire, about 3 km from the centre. Kon K’Tu village is about 5 km from the centre, across the bridge. Walk the deck when it is steady. Go Vietnam lists the crossing on foot as free. A travel page prints 5,000 VND for a motorbike, and the provincial portal does not print that toll. Check on arrival.

The prison museum sits in the same centre. Go Vietnam prints 30,000 VND and about ninety minutes for the French-era cells. The Kon Tum provincial portal does not print a matching fee. Check on arrival at the gate. The provincial museum holds the gong-heritage displays the portal links to the UNESCO listing of the Central Highlands gong space. A ticket and hours for that museum are Check on arrival. Lunch or dinner can be gỏi lá on Trần Cao Vân. VietnamNet describes forest and garden leaves, boiled pork, shrimp, and a fermented rice and dried-shrimp sauce. The leaf count is not one figure. Cơm lam, glutinous rice grilled in bamboo, is the village lunch Go Vietnam names for the Ba Na and Xơ Đăng, eaten with grilled chicken. The evening drink is coffee. Vietnam Tourism calls the café the social hub and describes cups overlooking the Đăk Bla.

Stay if the church, the bridge, and the villages are the reason. Go to Da Lat if you wanted a cooler hill station. Mang Den is about 54 km northeast on National Highway 24, the pine plateau Vietnam Tourism describes with lakes and waterfalls. The minutes are Check on arrival. Chu Mom Ray is the border rainforest park on the Vietnam Tourism province list. The drive time is Check on arrival. Pleiku is the flight, not the night in town.
gettingAround: Fly into Pleiku Airport (PXU). FlightConnections shows nonstop domestic flights from Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City on Vietnam Airlines and VietJet Air. kontumtourism.com prints nearly 45 km and about one hour by bus or taxi from Pleiku to Kon Tum city. Travelmath prints 51 km from Pleiku to the old Kontum airport code, and about 299 km by road from Da Nang. Fares for the Pleiku transfer are Check on arrival. Neither page lists a passenger airport in Kon Tum.

kontumtourism.com also prints the long buses: about eight hours and about 180,000–200,000 VND from Da Nang, about twelve hours and about 220,000–300,000 VND from Ho Chi Minh City, and about twenty-five hours and about 600,000–650,000 VND from Hanoi. Those figures sit on that publisher alone. Check on arrival.

In town, the church, the prison, and the provincial museum are a walk in the centre. Go Vietnam puts the city cluster within about 10 km. Kon Klor’s communal house is about 3 km out, and Kon K’Tu is about 5 km across the bridge. A motorbike or a taxi covers that. Minutes and fares are Check on arrival. After the loop, Vietnam Tourism describes the cafés as the social hub, with coffee rather than a club quarter. Drink prices are Check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: Central Kon Tum
stayAreas.summary: Sleep near Nguyen Hue if the church morning and the river afternoon are the day. The rooms are guesthouses and small hotels, not a resort strip.

eat: Breakfast is phở khô, dry noodles in one bowl and hot broth in the other. Go Vietnam puts the morning shops at about 6:00 to 10:00, around the market, at about 20,000–33,000 VND, or up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl. Gỏi lá is the leaf platter on Trần Cao Vân. The leaf count and the platter price are not one figure. Cơm lam and grilled chicken are the village pair, and those prices disagree too.
interestsBody: The timber church on Nguyen Hue is the reason to stop. Kon Klor and Kon K’Tu are the river afternoon, about 3 km and about 5 km from the centre.
The prison museum is the history morning in the same centre. Gong displays sit at the provincial museum, and the evening is coffee, with the Đăk Bla in front of the cafés Vietnam Tourism describes.

blocks.heading: The wooden church
paragraphs: The Kon Tum provincial portal places the cathedral on Nguyen Hue in Thống Nhất ward. It was built from 1913 to 1918 in cà chít timber, with Roman lines and Ba Na roof forms. Go Vietnam lists free entry and Sunday Mass at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00. Visitor hours outside Mass are Check on arrival. Allow about an hour, and walk from hotels in the centre.

blocks.heading: Kon Klor and Kon K’Tu
paragraphs: Kon Klor’s cable bridge opened on 1 May 1994 and runs 292 metres over the Đăk Bla. Go Vietnam’s cluster page and its communal-house page both print that length. The hall beside the river is the large Ba Na nhà rông, rebuilt after the 2010 fire, about 3 km from the centre. Kon K’Tu is about 5 km from the centre, across the bridge. Go Vietnam lists the walk as free, free entry to the village, and a village visit of two to three hours. Workshop or performance fees are Check on arrival. A travel page prints 5,000 VND for a motorbike on the bridge. The provincial portal does not print that toll. Cross when the deck is steady.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Two-bowl phở around the market, gỏi lá on Trần Cao Vân, and cơm lam with grilled chicken.

cards.title: Wooden church
cards.summary: Romanesque timber cathedral built 1913–1918 in cà chít wood on Nguyen Hue. About one hour. Go Vietnam lists free entry. Sunday Mass is 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00.

interestGroups.title: Prison museum
interestGroups.summary: French-era cells in the centre, then the provincial museum if gong culture is why you came.

blocks.heading: Kon Tum Prison
paragraphs: Go Vietnam prints 30,000 VND and about ninety minutes for the French-era cells. The Kon Tum provincial portal does not print a matching fee or a clock. Check on arrival. The visit is colonial prison history. Go in the morning, on foot from the centre.

blocks.heading: Gongs and the museum
paragraphs: The provincial museum holds the gong-heritage bank the Kon Tum portal links to the UNESCO listing of the Central Highlands gong space. Hours and a ticket are Check on arrival. The Culture, Sports and Tourism Week brings gong performances for about five to six days. The portal does not print a fixed date. Pơ Thi, the Ba Na new-year ritual, falls in the 12th lunar month in villages including Kon K’Tu. Check on arrival.

cards.title: Kon Tum Prison
cards.summary: A French-era prison museum in the city centre. Allow about an hour and a half. Go Vietnam prints 30,000 VND. The provincial portal does not print that fee. Check on arrival.

season.label: Drier months
season.note: Go Vietnam calls November to April the drier window and says June to September rain can make forest side-trip roads slippery. That is guidance, not a closure. The Culture, Sports and Tourism Week runs about five to six days, and the Kon Tum provincial portal does not print a fixed date. Pơ Thi falls in the 12th lunar month. Check on arrival.

faqs.a: Fly to Pleiku (PXU). kontumtourism.com and FlightConnections treat it as the highland gateway, and neither lists a passenger airport in Kon Tum. kontumtourism.com prints nearly 45 km and about one hour by road. Travelmath prints 51 km. Fares are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: Is the wooden church the same visit as Kon K’Tu?
faqs.a: No. The church is on Nguyen Hue in Thống Nhất ward. Kon K’Tu is a Ba Na village about 5 km from the centre, across the Kon Klor bridge. The church is about an hour. Go Vietnam prints two to three hours for the village.

faqs.q: What does the prison museum cost?
faqs.a: Go Vietnam prints 30,000 VND. The Kon Tum provincial portal does not print a matching fee. Check on arrival at the gate. Allow about an hour and a half.

faqs.q: Where is breakfast, and where is the evening?
faqs.a: Breakfast is phở khô near the market, about 6:00 to 10:00. Go Vietnam prints about 20,000–33,000 VND a bowl, or up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl. The evening drink is coffee. Vietnam Tourism describes the highland bean as Robusta and does not print a cup price. Go Vietnam’s cluster article prints 25,000–40,000 VND for an arabica cup, and 30,000–60,000 VND in Măng Đen. Check on arrival.
